evidence.finding: node1's OS hostname was 'vm-rhel10-1922825936' (the VM's autogenerated name, /etc/hostname contained 'localhost'), not 'node1', while its IP 10.100.237.10 matched the expected node1 role.

dhcpcd.conf comment 'Request a hostname from the network' with active udhcpc/dhcpcd process, and no 'nohook hostname' entry present yet — meaning DHCP renewals could keep overwriting any manually set hostname.

Cluster had 4 members: rabbit@vm-rhel10-1922825936, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3, plus a duplicate listing of rabbit@vm-rhel10-1922825936 as the running node1 — i.e. node1 joined the RabbitMQ cluster under the wrong Erlang node name before its hostname was corrected.

Executor stopped rabbitmq-server, set /etc/hostname to 'node1', ran 'hostname node1', and added 'nohook hostname' to dhcpcd.conf — this is the corrective sequence, but no subsequent record in the selected audit shows rabbitmq-server being restarted or the node successfully rejoining the cluster under the new name.

SSH from node1 to node2 and node3 both failed with 'Permission denied (publickey,password,keyboard-interactive)' immediately after CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY was appended to each node's authorized_keys — pubkey auth did not work despite the setup steps matching the platform primer's documented pattern.

A custom iptables chain RMQ_MGMT was in place, ACCEPTing only the three cluster node IPs (10.100.237.10/11/12) and DROPping everything else for the management port — this part of the requirement (mgmt reachable only within cluster) appears to have been implemented before the timeout.

Executor was killed by a hard timeout after 1200s (claude-code timed out); no structured completion report was produced, so there is no confirmation that CA-issued client-cert enforcement was ever configured or tested.

likely_causes.cause: node1's default OS hostname didn't match its intended cluster identity ('node1') and DHCP was configured to re-assert a network-supplied hostname on lease renewal, causing RabbitMQ to boot and join the cluster under a spurious Erlang node name (rabbit@vm-rhel10-...) before this was caught and partially fixed.

Cleaning up the resulting bad cluster membership (stopping rabbitmq, renaming host, needing to rejoin/forget the stale node) consumed a large share of the 20-minute budget, leaving insufficient time to reach the TLS/CA-specific work (CA generation, per-node certs, mTLS enforcement) or to verify it.

Broken passwordless inter-node SSH (pubkey auth rejected on node2/node3 despite following the documented CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY setup) likely forced the executor into slower per-node manual file distribution for CA/cert material, adding further delay.

The executor may not have re-started rabbitmq-server on node1 after the hostname fix within the visible window, meaning the final state of the cluster (and thus TLS/mTLS enforcement) is unverified at termination.

next_attempt_guidance: Before installing or starting rabbitmq-server on any node, explicitly set /etc/hostname to the intended name (node1/node2/node3) via 'hostname <name>' and 'echo <name> > /etc/hostname', and add 'nohook hostname' to /etc/dhcpcd.conf immediately — do this as step zero, not as a mid-stream fix, to avoid RabbitMQ ever joining the cluster under an autogenerated VM hostname.
Verify hostname/identity with 'hostname; cat /etc/hostname; hostname -f 2>/dev/null' on all three nodes before starting the rabbitmq-server service anywhere.

Test inter-node SSH (ssh -v node2 true) right after key setup and inspect verbose output before relying on it; if pubkey auth is rejected, don't loop on SSH debugging — fall back to the primer's base64/heredoc paste-per-node pattern or an http.server transfer for distributing the CA and per-node certs.

If a node has already joined the RabbitMQ cluster under a wrong node name, use 'rabbitmqctl forget_cluster_node rabbit@<wrongname>' on a healthy node before re-adding it under the corrected name, rather than restarting alone.

Generate the CA and per-node certs early, and keep a running checklist (CA created, node certs issued, rabbitmq.conf ssl_options + peer verification configured, mgmt interface firewalled, and finally a live TLS connection test with and without a CA-issued client cert) so partial progress under a time budget is easy to resume or report — the mgmt-only-firewall step (iptables RMQ_MGMT chain) was completed, but there is no evidence CA/mTLS enforcement was ever reached or tested.

Given the timeout, budget the hostname/identity and SSH sanity checks to a few minutes; if they aren't resolved quickly, proceed with the TLS/CA work using single-node manual cert distribution rather than continuing to debug cluster SSH.
summary: The attempt timed out at 1200s without a structured completion report. The redacted evidence shows two intertwined infrastructure problems that likely consumed most of the time budget before the actual TLS/CA task could be finished and verified: (1) node1 booted with a mismatched OS hostname ('vm-rhel10-...' instead of 'node1') with DHCP configured to keep reasserting a network-supplied hostname, causing RabbitMQ to join the cluster under the wrong node identity — this was caught and a fix sequence (stop service, set hostname, add dhcpcd nohook) was started, but no subsequent record confirms rabbitmq-server was restarted or the node rejoined cleanly; and (2) inter-node SSH pubkey authentication failed on first attempt from node1 to node2/node3 despite following the documented key-setup steps, which may have forced slower manual per-node file distribution for certificate material. One requirement — restricting the management interface to cluster-internal IPs — does appear to have been implemented (an iptables RMQ_MGMT chain accepting only the three node IPs and dropping the rest). There is no evidence in the available records that CA creation, per-node TLS certificate issuance, or client-certificate-only AMQP authentication was ever configured or tested before the timeout.</summary>
